newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property stocks dive 5 pct on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property stocks dive 5 pct on rumours.

text.p: Singapore property stocks dived on Friday with the SES property index plunging 5.27 percent, or 37.84 points, to 680.70 on rumours the government would announce sweeping changes to the public housing market.
Property counters, especially in firms with a heavy exposure to the residential property market, fell in heavy selling.
City Developments, DBS Land and Wing Tai Holdings touched new 1997 lows of S$12.00, S$4.74 and S$3.88 respectively before rebounding slightly at the close.
The property index came off its low to close 5.06 percent down at 682.19.
Analysts said some of the changes could include higher interest rates for buyers who want to upgrade to a bigger public housing unit.
The other rumour was that owners would have to stay longer in their public housing units before being allowed to sell them.
A property analyst said the changes would have an adverse impact on the prices of private housing as the two markets are linked.
A HDB spokeswoman told Reuters that National Development Minister Lim Hng Kiang would hold a news conference at 11 a.m. (0300 GMT) on Saturday.
She said the conference would be open only to local media and refused to say what it would address.
